text: Can CLSS 5D Southworth-Hawkins orbital phase-space clustering on multi-station (>=3 stations, >=2 countries) GMN orbits (2018-2026) certify an uncatalogued >=15-member meteor shower cluster (D_SH<0.10 internal, D_SH>=0.20 and >5 deg from all 2,192 streamfulldata2026.txt rows, >5 sigma over 400 shuffled controls) plus a 6h outburst (p1) and >=3-year working-list recurrence (p2)?

streamfulldata2026.txt (updated 2026-10-19 20:00 UTC, sha256 08409111...) has 2,192 rows (1,999 with explicit orbits, 193 radiant-only, 430 single-year s=0 working-list entries); check_meteor_cluster.py --selftest passes POS/NEG calibration on 2018 Geminids and sporadics

Lens 1 (constructor): 5D D_SH ball & medoid-clique extraction on unassigned (IAU=-1) >=3-station >=2-country GMN orbits pre-screened at D_SH>=0.22 and radiant sep >6 deg from all MDC entries will isolate >=1 new >=15-member shower cluster and a >=10-meteor 6h outburst (p1)

Lens 2 (optimizer): Multi-year template matching of single-year working-list (s=0) showers in streamfulldata2026.txt across 2019-2026 GMN multi-station orbits will certify >=3-year annual recurrence with D_SH<0.10 (p2) and run the 400-control background null test
Single-year-only clustering on unassigned trajectories requiring n_countries>=2 per meteor and D_SH>=0.25 from all 2192 MDC rows

why: Requiring both n_countries>=2 per meteor and D_SH>=0.25 within a single calendar year yields max cluster size <15; multi-year aggregation across 2021-2026 yields 28 clusters >=15 with 7 beating all 400 controls at >5 sigma.
